title: The Donation Box with Two Lists
title_ja: 二つの一覧がある寄付箱
fact_notes: 人物、具体的な出来事・実験・記録は架空の教材例。実在の調査や統計の結果ではない。参考リンクは制作台帳であり外部の実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: Students at a Japanese high school organized a donation campaign after arranging an online exchange with a partner school overseas.
sentences.ja: 日本の高校の生徒たちは海外の交流校とのオンライン交流を設定した後、寄付活動を企画した。

sentences.en: They hoped to support an after-school reading program that the partner school was planning for children in its neighborhood.
sentences.ja: 交流校が近隣の子どもたちのために計画していた放課後の読書活動を支援したかった。

sentences.en: The group initially collected used English storybooks, believing that a large number of books would naturally be helpful.
sentences.ja: 当初は本の数が多ければ当然役立つと考え、中古の英語の物語本を集めた。

sentences.en: Within a week, several boxes had been filled with books that students and their families were willing to give away.
sentences.ja: 1週間以内に、生徒や家族が譲りたい本で箱がいくつもいっぱいになった。

sentences.en: Before arranging delivery, the teacher suggested asking the partner school which materials it actually needed for the reading program.
sentences.ja: 配送を手配する前に、教師は読書活動に実際に必要な教材を交流校に尋ねるよう提案した。

sentences.en: The teachers overseas explained that they already had many books for older children but needed simpler materials for beginning readers.
sentences.ja: 海外の教師たちは年長の子ども向けの本はすでに多くあるが、読み始めたばかりの子ども向けの簡単な教材が必要だと説明した。

sentences.en: They also mentioned that storage space was limited and that receiving too many unsuitable books could create additional work.
sentences.ja: 保管場所が限られ、不適切な本を大量に受け取ると余分な作業が生じる可能性も述べた。

sentences.en: The Japanese students realized that their generous intentions did not automatically guarantee that the proposed donation would meet local needs.
sentences.ja: 日本の生徒たちは善意だけでは予定の寄付が現地の必要性を満たすと保証できないことに気づいた。

sentences.en: Instead of sending everything immediately, the two schools created a shared list of materials that would be useful to the program.
sentences.ja: すぐに全部送る代わりに、両校は活動に役立つ教材の共通一覧を作成した。

sentences.en: A second list described the books that were already available in the donation boxes, including information about their reading difficulty.
sentences.ja: 二つ目の一覧には寄付箱にすでにある本とその読解難度についての情報を記載した。

sentences.en: The students compared the two lists and selected a smaller collection that the partner school had specifically requested.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは二つの一覧を比較し、交流校が具体的に希望したより少量の本を選んだ。

sentences.en: They decided to offer the remaining books at a local exchange event rather than discard them or send them unnecessarily.
sentences.ja: 残った本は捨てたり不要な配送をしたりせず、地元の交換会で提供することにした。

sentences.en: The receiving teachers later asked whether the Japanese students could also create short recordings to accompany some of the selected stories.
sentences.ja: 受け入れ側の教師は後に、選んだ物語の一部に添える短い録音も作成できるか尋ねた。

sentences.en: After confirming permission to record the relevant material, the students prepared audio files for the stories that could be used.
sentences.ja: 該当教材を録音する許可を確認した後、利用可能な物語の音声ファイルを作成した。

sentences.en: This additional contribution had not been part of the original plan, but it emerged through communication between the two schools.
sentences.ja: この追加の協力は最初の計画になかったが、両校のやり取りから生まれた。

sentences.en: The two groups agreed to discuss the usefulness of the materials again after the reading program had been running for a while.
sentences.ja: 活動開始からしばらく経った後、教材の有用性を再度話し合うことに合意した。

sentences.en: The campaign changed the students' understanding of international cooperation because they began to view the receiving school as a partner.
sentences.ja: 寄付活動は生徒の国際協力への理解を変えた。受け入れ側を対等な協力相手と考え始めたからだ。

sentences.en: They learned that the quantity of donated objects was less important than whether the objects served a purpose identified by local people.
sentences.ja: 寄付品の量よりも、現地の人が明らかにした目的に役立つかどうかの方が重要だと学んだ。

sentences.en: Listening to the partner school did not reduce the value of their contribution; it helped them direct their efforts more effectively.
sentences.ja: 交流校の話を聞くことは協力の価値を下げるのではなく、努力をより効果的に向ける助けとなった。

sentences.en: For these students, meaningful cooperation became a process of asking, adjusting, and learning together rather than simply giving something away.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちにとって意義ある協力とは、単に物を譲るのでなく共に尋ね、調整し、学ぶ過程になった。

questions.prompt: What did the students want to support?
questions.explanation_ja: 放課後の読書活動を支援したかった。

questions.prompt: What did the overseas teachers say they needed?
options: More books for older children only.
Books about the Japanese students' families.
questions.explanation_ja: 初学者向けの簡単な教材。

questions.prompt: How could too many unsuitable books create problems?
options: They would make reading free for everyone.
They would take space and require extra work.
They would eliminate the need for storage.
questions.explanation_ja: 保管場所と作業負担の問題。

questions.prompt: Why did the schools create two lists?
options: To rank students by English grades.
To compare the prices of schools.
To match the requested materials with the available books.
questions.explanation_ja: 希望と既存の寄付品を照合した。

questions.prompt: What happened to the remaining books?
options: They were all immediately thrown away.
They were to be offered at a local exchange event.
questions.explanation_ja: 地元の交換会で提供すると決めた。

questions.prompt: What did the students confirm before preparing recordings?
options: Permission to record the relevant material.
The size of each donation box.
A new date for school examinations.

questions.explanation_ja: 協力の案がやり取りから生まれた。

questions.prompt: Why was further discussion planned after the program began?
options: To learn whether the materials were useful in practice.
To decide which school had won a competition.
To increase donations regardless of need.
questions.explanation_ja: 実際に役立ったかを確認するため。

options: Sending more objects always improves the impact of a donation.
Donors should decide everything without consulting recipients.
International cooperation is limited to collecting books.
Cooperation should respond to priorities identified by the people receiving support.
questions.explanation_ja: 受け入れ側の必要性に応じた協力が重要。

discourse.role_ja: 教材不足に加えて保管問題を示す。
当初の配送方針から変更した行動。

paraphrases.source: They hoped to support an after-school reading program that the partner school was planning for children in its neighborhood.
paraphrases.rewrite: They wanted to help a reading activity the overseas school intended to offer local children after classes.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 現地の子ども向け読書活動を支援したかった。

paraphrases.source: They also mentioned that storage space was limited and that receiving too many unsuitable books could create additional work.
paraphrases.rewrite: They added that limited storage made a large shipment of unsuitable books potentially burdensome.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 保管場所が狭いので不適切な本の大量受領は負担になり得る。

paraphrases.source: They decided to offer the remaining books at a local exchange event rather than discard them or send them unnecessarily.
paraphrases.rewrite: They chose to make the other books available locally instead of throwing them away or shipping them when they were not needed.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 残りは地元で活用することにした。

paraphrases.source: They learned that the quantity of donated objects was less important than whether the objects served a purpose identified by local people.
paraphrases.rewrite: They understood that how well the items met a locally identified need mattered more than how many items were given.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 量より現地の必要性への適合が大切。
